questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When you are traveling through an intersection.
When you are passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When you are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that hospital emergency services are located to the right.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the lane is clear.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.
A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
A driver must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
A driver may turn in the direction the red arrow is pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says otherwise, a red arrow means you must stop completely and wait until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. Yellow lines separate lanes going in opposite directions.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It makes you feel too confident.
It affects your thinking ability.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, makes you overconfident, and impairs your thinking. It also harms your vision and ability to judge distance.

questions.question: Which of these is true about cell phone use while driving?

options.text: Drivers under 18 cannot text or talk on a cell phone while driving.
Drivers 18 and older must use a hands-free device when talking on a cell phone.
Drivers 18 and older cannot text while driving.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, drivers under 18 cannot talk or text on a cell phone while driving. Drivers 18 and older must use a hands-free device when using a cell phone.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly and carefully.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and drive carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead—they light the road better in fog.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, who goes first?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver can proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: What is true about large vehicles' blind spots?

options.text: They have larger blind spots.
They have smaller blind spots.
They have no blind spots.
They have the same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the rear that you cannot see in their mirrors.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before you go.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before you go.
questions.explanation: At a crossing with multiple tracks, do not move as soon as one train passes. Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let traffic in the intersection or on the road you are entering go first.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You are less alert.
You become calmer and can focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You become calmer and can focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time, makes it harder to see clearly, messes up your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you calm down or concentrate better.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turns allowed.
U-turns are allowed.
Winding road ahead.
Sharp left turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means something is not allowed. This sign means U-turns are not permitted.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the other vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you have to drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the other vehicle is turning left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right when there is a passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Nothing, because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
They can get a ticket.
They will always get just a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as drivers. Bicyclists who break traffic laws can be ticketed just like drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn lane.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign means U-turns are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line of cars at a stop sign. When the cars ahead pass through and there is no other traffic, what must you do?

options.text: You can go through without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
You can roll slowly past the stop sign.
You can follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before going. Do not feel rushed by other cars to skip this stop.

questions.question: When can you go through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and making sure it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and making sure it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before entering the intersection at a stop sign, even if there is no stop line or crosswalk. Once you have stopped completely, you can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful where children are playing. Children may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: When two drivers arrive at a four-way stop intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, give the right-of-way to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When must you yield to a stopped transit bus that is re-entering traffic?

options.text: Only if there are cars behind you.
If the bus has turned on its hazard lights.
When the bus has its turn signal on and a flashing "Yield" sign is lit.
Never. The bus must wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the bus has its turn signal on and a flashing "Yield" sign is lit.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a stopped transit bus when the driver signals to merge back into traffic and a flashing "Yield" sign appears on the bus. Slow down or move over to let the bus safely enter the traffic lane.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Some crossings do not have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs that show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background.
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.
White letters or symbols on a blue background.
White letters or symbols on a green background.

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Construction zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is taking place.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is taking place.
questions.explanation: Orange signs show construction, maintenance, or emergency work. They have black symbols on them.

questions.question: What is a good rule to remember about passing?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic to see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the chance of a crash. If you drive faster than other traffic, you will have to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, obey speed limits, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic signal light?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, what must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right sides.
